Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

however adverb

but, nevertheless

also nevertheless, all the same, though, yet, but yet, still

classical

Cic. Att. 12.41.1: scīre tamen volēbam ubi essēs
Cic. Fam. 9.20.2: sine pāvōne tamen
Hor. Ep. 1.10.24

tamen

adverb; at the head of its clause or after the word it stresses

however, nevertheless, all the same

The “however” that answers a concession, said or understood (etsī, quamquam, quamvīs, cum): “even so”. With sed or at, “but yet”: sed tamen.

Other words

  • autem — however, but, on the other hand

    conjunction; never first in its clause, but after its first word or phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.18.2: maximē autem date operam ut valeātis; Traupman 330

    A light “but” that sets one thing beside another, not “nevertheless”; where nothing is set against it, leave it out.

  • vērumtamen (vērum tamen) — but even so, however

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 6.2.2: est magnum illud quidem vērum tamen multiplex puerī ingenium; Cic. Rosc. Am. 55 (Lewis & Short)

  • nihilōminus (nihilō minus) — nonetheless, none the less

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.51: nihilō minus ipsī lūcet; Cato Agr. 39.2: nihilō minus sūmptum futūrum

Examples

  • nihil erat quod scrīberem. scīre tamen volēbam ubi essēs

    I had nothing to write; however, I wanted to know where you wereCic. Att. 12.41.1

  • etiam Hirtiō cēnam dedī, sine pāvōne tamen

    I even gave Hirtius dinner, without a peacock, howeverCic. Fam. 9.20.2

  • nātūram expellēs furcā, tamen ūsque recurret

    drive nature out with a pitchfork, and she will keep coming back all the sameHor. Ep. 1.10.24

  • nōn dubia est Ithacī prūdentia, sed tamen optat fūmum dē patriīs posse vidēre focīs

    no one doubts the Ithacan’s good sense, but yet he longs to see the smoke rise from his own country’s hearthsOv. Pont. 1.3.33–34

See also however.
